Select the Optimal Dose Combination of BOIN-ETC Trials

Source: R/boin_etc_select_obd.R
boin_etc_select_obd.Rd

Select the optimal dose combination (ODC) of one or more trials of the BOIN-ETC design of Kakizume et al. (2024) from their final data. The DLT rates are made monotone along both drugs by bivariate isotonic regression, the maximum tolerated dose combination (MTDC) of every row bounds the candidates of that row, and the ODC is the candidate with the highest estimated utility.

Usage

boin_etc_select_obd(
  n_pts,
  n_tox,
  n_resp,
  n_tox_resp = NULL,
  target,
  psi00 = 40,
  psi11 = 60,
  utility_prior = c(1, 1),
  odc_tie = c("lowest", "all"),
  cutoff_eli = 0.95,
  p_eli = NULL,
  excluded = NULL,
  early_stop = NULL
)

Arguments

n_pts, n_tox, n_resp

Numeric matrices for a single trial, with one row per level of drug A and one column per level of drug B, or arrays with dimensions trial by level of drug A by level of drug B, of the patients treated, the DLTs and the responses.

n_tox_resp

Array or matrix of the same size, or NULL. Patients with both a DLT and a response. Needed only when psi00 + psi11 is not 100. Defaults to NULL.

target

Numeric scalar. Target DLT probability, phi.

psi00, psi11

Numeric scalars from 0 to 100. Utilities of a patient with neither a DLT nor a response and with both; a response without DLT scores 100 and a DLT without response 0. Default to 40 and 60, the utilities (100, 40, 60, 0) of Kakizume et al. (2024).

utility_prior

Numeric vector of two positive numbers. Beta prior of the utility of a combination divided by 100. Defaults to c(1, 1).

odc_tie

Character scalar. How tied candidates are reported: "lowest" (the default) selects the one with the lowest sum of the two levels; "all" also marks every tied candidate in tied, which sim_boin_etc then counts as selected, as Kakizume et al. (2024) do. The ODC returned in obd_a and obd_b is the same in both cases.

cutoff_eli, p_eli

As in boin_etc_simulate. Used only when excluded is NULL.

excluded

Logical array or matrix of the same size, or NULL. Combinations excluded by the DLT rule during the trial (component excluded of boin_etc_simulate), which are never selected. Defaults to NULL: a combination is excluded when its own final DLT data fail the rule of cutoff_eli.

early_stop

Logical vector or NULL. Trials stopped early, which select no ODC. Defaults to NULL, no trial.

Value

A list with components

obd_a, obd_b

Integer vectors, the levels of drug A and drug B of the ODC of every trial (NA when none is selected).

n_tied

Integer vector, the number of tied candidates.

tied

Logical array, the tied candidates of every trial (with odc_tie = "lowest", only the selected ODC).

mtd_col

Integer matrix, trial by level of drug A, the level of drug B of the MTDC of every row.

reason

Character vector: "selected", "early_stop" or "no_admissible_dose".

tox_est

Array of the isotonic estimates of the DLT rates.

utility

Array of the estimated utilities of the tried combinations, on the scale 0 to 100.

Details

The DLT rate of every combination, tried or not, is estimated by (y + 0.05) / (n + 0.1) (the beta(0.05, 0.05) posterior mean of Kakizume et al., 2024) and made non-decreasing in both levels by the unweighted least-squares fit of bivariate isotonic regression, as in the code of the authors (Iso::biviso() without weights), computed by the algorithm of Dykstra and Robertson (1982) until no estimate changes by 1e-13 in a cycle. In every row (level of drug A) the MTDC is the combination whose estimate is closest to target; among combinations within 1e-8 of the smallest distance, which are tied in exact arithmetic, the highest level of drug B. The candidates are the tried combinations that are not excluded and not above the MTDC of their row.

The utility of a candidate is estimated by 100 * (q + a) / (n + a + b), with (a, b) the utility_prior and the quasi-binomial number of events q = (100 x + psi00 (n - y - x) + (psi00 + psi11 - 100) z) / 100 of n patients with y DLTs, x responses and z both, the estimate of the code of the authors (Kakizume et al., 2024, do not state it). The ODC is the candidate with the highest estimate; the candidates within 1e-6 of it are tied, and the one with the lowest sum of the levels, then the first in column-major order, is selected.

The code of the authors also lets untried combinations (utility 50) and excluded ones be selected, and counts every tied combination; on the published trials, leaving out the untried ones changes the selection of 0.0 to 0.3 0.14 errors of about 1e-6, so that which of tied MTDCs it takes depends on them; the published percentages of trials selecting a correct ODC are on average about 1 point lower than with exact ties (see inst/reproduce/reproduce_Kakizume2024.R).

References

Kakizume, T., Takeda, K., Taguri, M. and Morita, S. (2024). BOIN-ETC: A Bayesian optimal interval design considering efficacy and toxicity to identify the optimal dose combinations. Statistical Methods in Medical Research, 33(4), 716-727. doi:10.1177/09622802241236936

Dykstra, R. L. and Robertson, T. (1982). An algorithm for isotonic regression for two or more independent variables. The Annals of Statistics, 10(3), 708-716. doi:10.1214/aos/1176345866

See also

sim_boin_etc, boin_etc_simulate

Examples

n_pts <- matrix(c(3, 6, 0, 9, 6, 3), nrow = 2)
n_tox <- matrix(c(0, 1, 0, 2, 2, 2), nrow = 2)
n_resp <- matrix(c(0, 2, 0, 5, 4, 2), nrow = 2)
boin_etc_select_obd(n_pts, n_tox, n_resp, target = 0.30)

#>
